1.mascotDialogue: No comparisons anywhere in this algorithm — none at all. Only repeatedly asking, 'which bucket does this digit belong to,' and gathering the buckets back, in order, digit by digit.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 10's backward loop — this is what keeps radix sort stable. Processing the original array from the end preserves the relative order of elements sharing the same digit.

3.mascotDialogue: 170 and 90 both arrive in bucket 0 this pass, and their order — 170 before 90 — remains exactly as it was. This is stability, performing its duty quietly, across every pass.

4.mascotDialogue: This is why loop direction matters, even though it appears a harmless stylistic choice — radix sort's correctness across passes depends on every single pass being stable, not merely correct on its own. Maa... ganbatte ne.
